policy.existingCoverage: Secure canonical identity or an already-resolved variant match is counted as existing coverage.
policy.parentReuse: A gallery or institution physically housed in an already canonical building is routed to parent enrichment where a second marker would duplicate the same physical place.
policy.privateCommercialDeferral: Private, commercial, sales-led, recently opened or coordinate-unstable gallery listings are not automatic canonical gaps. They remain deferred under the existing gallery policy until a consistent framework resolves longevity, cultural significance, independent place identity and coordinate stability.
policy.newCandidate: Durable member organisations, artist-run or foundation-based institutions, long-running non-commercial exhibition spaces, and distinctive public cultural sites may proceed to individual identity and coordinate audits.
policy.coordinateOnlyBacklog: Scope is approved but production is blocked only by the absence of a distinct non-guessed physical anchor.
policy.geographicOutOfScope: The source listing is outside Oslo municipality and is not an Oslo gallery production gap. Existing canonical coverage elsewhere is preserved where applicable.

researchNotes.machineAudit: PR #3516 established 18 exact canonical matches and a 48-item manual queue. Its fuzzy and proximity candidates were treated only as leads, never as identity proof.
researchNotes.priorityTranchePolicy: The merged curated gallery scope established that VisitOSLO presence alone does not create a canonical gap and that private/commercial galleries must be handled consistently.
researchNotes.manualResolution: The manual pass applied the same policy to all 66 source items and separately resolved clear parent-building reuse cases.

productionClosure.policy: Do not invent offsets or choose an unnamed nearby entrance by proximity. ROM and SOFT remain approved scope items but are withheld from canonical production until a distinct authoritative entrance/building object is available.
